steps.title: Climb only as high as the job needs
steps.body:
The nine rungs run from the cheapest change to the most dangerous. For each one the table gives an example, where it lives in the repository, the rebuild time, how it fails and the way back.

The rule: use the lowest-numbered rung that can do the job.

steps.title: Rung 1: your program is the safest change
steps.body: A hook in `scripts/rootfs/` runs your program at boot. A rebuild takes seconds, a failure is a failed service, and the way back is to edit and reboot.

steps.title: Rung 2: packages, users and config files
steps.body:
Add a package, a user or a file through `scripts/rootfs/` and the package lists. It takes a minute to rebuild.

If you break it, you may get no login and must re-flash the rootfs.

steps.title: Rungs 3 and 4: hardware description and kernel options
steps.body:
A device tree change (`custom/dts/`) enables a UART or I2C sensor in seconds; the way back is to boot the old `.dtb`. A kernel config fragment (`config/kernel/*.cfg`) enables a driver or feature in minutes with ccache.

A bad kernel config can mean no boot or a missing device, fixed by re-flashing `/boot`.

steps.title: Rung 5: kernel patches change code
steps.body:
A patch in `patches/kernel/` fixes or adds driver code and takes minutes to rebuild. Mistakes cause an oops or no boot.

Re-flash `/boot` to go back.

steps.title: Rung 6: bootloader environment
steps.body:
Boot order, console and kernel args live in `uEnv.txt`, `extlinux.conf` or the environment. It takes effect in seconds.

The failure is "no kernel found", fixed at the U-Boot prompt.

steps.title: Rungs 7 and 8: the boot chain itself
steps.body:
Bootloader patches (`patches/uboot/`, defconfig) can leave the board stopping at the ROM. Secure firmware (`patches/atf/`, optee) can leave **no serial output at all**.

Both need another medium or USB boot to recover.

steps.title: Rung 9: fuses cannot be undone
steps.body: Locking the board to signed images uses vendor tools and is not in this repository. Fuses are one-time, so a mistake means a bricked board, forever.

steps.anchor: Rung 1 is the cheapest to try, rung 9 cannot be undone. Rule of thumb: use the lowest-numbered rung that can do the job.
steps.title: Takeaway: lowest rung that works
steps.body: Every board directory has the same folders for these rungs (see `docs/board-contract.md`), so the answer to "where does this go?" is the same on every board.
